label: prop:hoefsmit-toroidal-ladder-locus
title: Toroidal locus of the Hoefsmit mixing ladder: $(n,\mu) = (d - \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{1}{2})$ is forced
html:
Let R be a field of characteristic zero and let \alpha, \beta \in R be constants. If the associated-Legendre order-ladder factor at degree n = d + \alpha and order \mu = \beta reproduces the squared Hoefsmit channel-mixing numerator identically in the axial distance d,

(d + \alpha - \beta)(d + \alpha + \beta + 1) \;=\; d^2 - 1
\qquad \text{for all } d \in R,

then

\alpha = -\tfrac{1}{2},
\qquad
\beta \in \bigl\{ \tfrac{1}{2},\; -\tfrac{3}{2} \bigr\},

i.e. (n, \mu) = \bigl(d - \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{1}{2}\bigr) up to the Legendre reflection \mu \mapsto -\mu - 1. The half-integer degree shift — the signature of the toroidal harmonic family P^\mu_{\nu - 1/2} — is forced by the Hoefsmit mixing structure, not imposed.

Context

The Hoefsmit seminormal block at axial distance d mixes the two lepton channels with amplitude b satisfying b^2 = [d-1]_q [d+1]_q / [d]_q^2 (prop:hoefsmit-binding-amplitude is the d = 2 meson case b^2 = [3]_q/[2]_q^2). At q \to 1 the squared mixing numerator is d^2 - 1. The associated-Legendre order-ladder factor is (n - \mu)(n + \mu + 1), and the toroidal harmonics — the separated eigenfunctions around a vortex ring [lebedev1965] — are exactly the Legendre family at half-integer degree \nu - \tfrac{1}{2} [whipple1917]. The proposition says the match between the two structures admits no freedom: the degree shift -\tfrac{1}{2} and the order \tfrac{1}{2} are the unique solution.

Because the q-bracket identity [d-1]_q[d+1]_q = [d]_q^2 - 1 holds for all q, the same forcing computation runs verbatim at the q-deformed level (the coefficient matching gives q^{2\alpha + 1} = 1); the half-integer shift survives q-deformation. The q-layer verification is recorded in the computational witness computations/substrate/hoefsmit-toroidal-ladder-probe.witness.json.

The physical reading: the two windings (\mu, \nu) of a toroidal harmonic P^\mu_{\nu-1/2}(\cosh\eta)\, e^{i\mu\theta} e^{i\nu\varphi} are the two local one-dimensional channel oscillations of a bound vortex pair, and the forced -\tfrac{1}{2} is the zero-point offset of the interpolating channel ladder.
